notes.title: Star Trek: Resurgence // Enhancement Update
notes.notes:
You asked, and we listened! The Resurgence [b]Enhancement Update[/b] is now on Steam with new features to enhance your experience aboard the [i]USS Resolute[/i].

[list]
[*] Achievements Engaged: Show off your skills and dedication with all-new achievements.
[/list]
[list]
[*] Choose from four graphics pre-sets: Minimum, Standard, High, and Maximum – tailor your game visuals to your taste and your system’s performance capabilities.
[/list]
[list]
[*] Take control of V-Sync: Toggle it on or off to find the perfect balance of smoothness and performance.
[/list]
[list]
[*] Enjoy enhanced performance across the board, including a smoother experience on Steam Deck.
[/list]

Your ongoing feedback is invaluable, and we can’t wait to hear what you think of these enhancements.

[b]Please note[/b]: Achievements can only be acquired via a NEW play-through of the game. So, now's the chance to make some different decisions to see what will happen to you and your crewmates aboard the Resolute! 

LLAP - The ST: R team

notes.title: Star Trek: Resurgence - Release Date Announced!
notes.notes:
We're pleased to announce that the U.S.S. Resolute and her crew will enter orbit on Steam on [b]May 23rd, 2024[/b]! Expect further incoming transmissions before that date: we'll reveal more in the coming weeks!

In the meantime, look out for new, extended interviews with Captain Riker himself, the legendary [b]Jonathan Frakes[/b], new behind-the-scenes content, and much more! 

We're so excited to finally bring our game to Steam - [b]Wishlist now![/b]  

[i][u]Did you know:[/u] Our game's hero ship the U.S.S. Resolute is named after the HMS Resolute, which was lost to the ice on an exploratory mission to arctic waters in 1854. The HMS [b]Enterprise[/b] was also part of that expedition. After an American whaler discovered the Resolute, it was restored and returned to the British who used timbers from the ship to construct the Resolute desk, which was presented to the United States as a gift of thanks. It is now located in the White House Oval Office and has been used by many Presidents of the United States.[/i]
